comments.body:
Work so far is in this branch

The Provider is picked up by JAX-RS, but it is not used. Rather the RdfStreamProvider is used. This makes me think you can only use one provider for each "type". But perhaps I am missing something.

I was wrong, I can now see that the MessageBodyWriter is stacking. So working from the RdfStream and getting to the Acl possibly using the stream.topic() and filtering to find the Acl.

However currently if you aren't an admin the Acl will be "inaccessibleResource", so that will have to be revised before this will be of any use.
Well done on this one, Jared Whiklo. Please update based on code review comments.
Updated and rebased changes for both PRs.

Resolved with:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/097714241c927bdc4ce9613bd6bec17dbb4d5b67 and
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/commit/6d7f196f1146378a171d81a44a8cb0454e068be8

Jared Whiklo, could you please document this "Link" feature as a note on this page:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Quick+Start+with+WebAC
I have added a note to the above page Andrew Woods. If you could take a look at it, I would appreciate it.

Jared Whiklo, I believe the LinkHeaderProvider needs to be configured in a spring.xml file for this functionality to work... maybe a snippet of how to do that configuration would be helpful in the wiki documentation.

I don't think it does require any configuration. Looking back at the commits that added it I don't see anything I added.

I think you might be thinking of the HttpHeaderPrincipalProvider that Peter Matthew Eichman created in https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-1790. That requires you to configure the delegate header in spring.
Hmm, when I spin up the 4.5.1-SNAPSHOT vagrant with audit and webac enabled, create a resource, then GET it... I am not seeing the "acl" Link header. Do you see it?

No, but that would be because unless you have added an ACL to that resource or a parent resource you won't get the Link Header.

In fact looking at what I did there, I am wondering if it would present the header if the ACL was on the parent resource. I'll have to try it but there could be a ticket to re-use the getEffectiveAcl code.
